chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I wrote to him, saying: Some of your mawali in Basra perform Ihram at Batan Al-Aqeeq, and there is no water in that place, nor any lodging, and the cost for them in that regard is severe. Their companions and their cameldrivers hasten them. And behind Batan Al-Aqeeq, by fifteen miles, there is a station wherein is water, and it is the station they are encamping in. So do you think they should perform Ihram from the place of water, for the ease it brings them and the lightness upon them?

He wrote back: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated the Miqat stations for their people and for those who come to them from other than their people. And in it is a concession (rukhsah) for the one who has an excuse (illah). Therefore, none should exceed the Miqat except for the one who has an excuse to do so.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.بَطْنُ الْعَقِيقِ: Batan Al-Aqeeq, a specific location near Mecca
key_terms.رُخْصَة: Concession or dispensation in Islamic law for those with a valid reason
key_terms.عِلَّة: Excuse or valid reason (e.g., illness, hardship) permitting deviation from the standard rule
key_terms.مَوَاقِيت: Miqat stations, the designated boundaries for entering the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Ihram at a location other than the designated Miqat due to hardship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms the Prophet’s designation of fixed Miqat stations while validating the concession (rukhsa) for those facing genuine hardship, such as the heavy costs and haste experienced by the Basrans at Bait al-Aqiq. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Miqat is the default obligation, but valid excuses permit crossing it prior to Ihram, balancing strict adherence with ease (yusr).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws, said, ‘I wrote to himasws Some of those in yourasws Wilayah in Al-Basra are wearing Ihraam at Batn Al-Aqeeq, and there is no water in that place, nor is there any lodging, and upon them regarding that requires intense provisions, and their companions and their cameleers hasten them; and from behind Batn Al-Aqeeq by fifteen miles, there is a station wherein is water, and it is their lodgement which they are encamping in. So what is yourasws view if they were to wear Ihraam from a place of water in order to be easier with them and light upon them’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> designated the junctures for its people and for the ones who come to it from other than its people, and with regards to it is a permission for the one who has a reason for it. Therefore, none should exceed the junctures except for the one who has a reason to do so’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following: “I once wrote to abu al-Hassan al-Rida’ ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

Certain people of your followers from Basrah assume the state of Ihram at Batn al-‘Aqiq. There is no water at that place or station. It makes things very difficult for them, their companions rush them as well as camel men. Fifteen miles after that place is a station, which has water where they disembark. If you consider it proper, instruct them to assume the state of Ihram at this place, which makes things easier for them.

He (the Imam) wrote, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, designated Mawaqit (places for assuming the state of Ihram) for their people as well as those who pass through them. However, there is permission for people who have difficulty and illness. It is not permissible to pass Miqat (place for assuming the state of Ihram) without acceptable reason (excuse).”’
